title: FHIR Feed Integration Operations
thesis: Snowflake turns daily facility-level FHIR feed activity from a synthetic regional health information exchange into feed completeness and data quality KPIs, 7-day interface incident risk scores, unmapped code anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables, with no patient data.

talking_points: Feed completeness, bundles accepted, bundle rejection rate and interface incidents for 40 facilities across 5 APJ markets.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to facility-day rows.
The issue-type chart shows which data quality issues turn into interface incidents and which are resolved without escalation.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of feed KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which facilities should interface operations look at first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each facility's probability of an interface incident in the next 7 days. It is an operational score, not a clinical prediction.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent 14 days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags unmapped code rate outliers per facility, and the forecast projects accepted bundles for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

talking_points: Conformance check compliance, FHIR profile conformance and pending profile reviews frame the integration gaps.
Check compliance against interface incidents by facility shows where missed checks and incidents move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised feed operations actions from the KPI, facility, issue-type and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a slow bundle delivery lands right now?

talking_points: Live bundle delivery events land in RAW.LIVE_BUNDLES, from the simulator or from S3 PutObject through Snowpipe. They carry facility-level metrics only, with no patient identifiers.
The Snowflake alert logs ALERT events with an SOP hint and the facility's current risk band, then emails the integration team.
tabs.call_out: From bundle delivery to follow-up in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 13 synthetic feed operations SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (S3, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic, facility-level demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
